fix(app): update xterm to prevent shared-atlas glyph corruption ### Linked issue Related to #6506 (wrong/fragmented-glyph reports) and #6424. Does not auto-close the umbrella issue. ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Enhancement - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Docs ### Reasoning Long-running TUIs can show fragments of the wrong glyphs even though the terminal buffer text is correct. Update xterm's WebGL renderer to the upstream atlas invalidation fixes rather than adding a periodic repaint workaround. - Pin `@xterm/xterm` to `6.1.0-beta.292` and `@xterm/addon-webgl` to `0.20.0-beta.291` (the latter requires core 292). - Add two real-WebGL pixel regressions through Paseo's production `TerminalEmulatorRuntime`: ordinary shared-atlas growth and explicit shared-atlas clearing. - Permit SwiftShader for headless browser CI. This flag is test-only; production WebGL behavior is unchanged. - Keep the lockfile change limited to these two dependencies. No runtime clearing/reloading workaround, daemon changes, native headless dependency update, or changes from the separate file-link PR. Evidence and complete regression source: https://github.com/getpaseo/paseo/issues/6506#issuecomment-6436600469 The old WebGL addon can retain obsolete glyph texture coordinates when atlas pages merge mid-frame, or skip a GPU texture upload when a replacement page's per-page version matches the previously bound page. Shared-atlas invalidation also needs to reach every renderer. The candidate contains [dc726a2](https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/commit/dc726a2ae628) and follow-ups [6042](https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/pull/6042), [6043](https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/pull/6043), [6055](https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/pull/6055). This reproduces and repairs a glyph-atlas failure class. It does not prove that all white bands, overlapping surfaces, GPU-context loss or monitor-scaling reports in the umbrella issue have this cause. Do not auto-close that issue based on this PR alone. ### Goals - Preserve the exact header pixels of both terminals throughout ordinary colored output and shared-atlas clearing, while keeping buffer text intact. - Fail on the old dependencies and pass on the updated pair with real WebGL. - Preserve existing terminal runtime, search and resize behavior. ### Non-goals - Fix every overlapping-frame/white-band symptom grouped under #6506. - Add window-refocus repairs, periodic clears, or disable WebGL. - Change the native headless renderer, daemon or unrelated file-link behavior. ### QA Base: `3a1b1466904a42d286f99641d1242d42e85f4f32`. The ordinary-output regression allocates its reference header after 16 output frames, then compares both terminals' header pixels during each of 256 renders. Buffer strings stay correct. There are no explicit clears, resizes, private xterm hooks or repair steps in this case. Actual Electron 44.2.0 / Chromium 152.0.7977.76, Apple M4 ANGLE Metal, DPR 2: | Probe | Old core 213 / WebGL 212 | Core 292 / WebGL 291 | |---|---:|---:| | Ordinary output: corrupted frames / 256 | 66 | 0 | | Maximum active-header channel mismatches | 29,322 | 0 | | Maximum sibling-header channel mismatches | 28,074 | 0 | | Separate explicit-clear sibling mismatches | 23,031 | 0 | Channel mismatches are not counts of distinct pixels. The old natural-output run ended on a clean frame, so per-frame checks are essential. After clean `npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund` and `npm run postinstall`: ```sh npm run test:browser --workspace=@getpaseo/app -- \ src/terminal/runtime/terminal-glyph-rendering.browser.test.ts \ src/terminal/runtime/terminal-emulator-runtime.browser.test.ts \ src/terminal/runtime/terminal-find.browser.test.ts \ src/terminal/runtime/terminal-resize-repro.browser.test.ts --bail=1 ``` ```text terminal-emulator-runtime.browser.test.ts 34 passed terminal-find.browser.test.ts 9 passed terminal-resize-repro.browser.test.ts 1 passed terminal-glyph-rendering.browser.test.ts 2 passed Test Files 4 passed (4) Tests 46 passed (46) ``` The two new cases fail with the original dependencies and pass with the candidate. App typecheck, targeted lint (0 errors/warnings), formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Existing runtime tests mock WebGL; the new rendering regressions and the separate Electron probe do not. | Platform | Coverage | |---|---| | Browser web | Real Chromium WebGL regression tests on macOS; SwiftShader permitted | | Desktop macOS | Isolated Electron production-terminal-runtime probe on actual Apple M4 GPU; not a packaged full-app smoke | | Desktop Windows / Linux | Not hardware-tested | | iOS / Android | Not tested; native headless dependency unchanged | Not yet verified: prolonged live-app use, sleep/wake, multi-monitor DPR transitions, performance benchmarks and CI on other OSes. The installed app and live daemon/terminals have not been modified or restarted. The public issue comment includes the full regression source and measured outputs. Local raw probe logs and synthetic screenshots are retained separately. Investigation and verification were agent-assisted; this has not yet been field-tested by the reporter in the installed app.
Actual Apple GPU screenshots: separate explicit shared-atlas-clear probe These synthetic screenshots contain no user terminal content. They show the **explicit-clear** case, not the transient ordinary-output case above. [nona] Intl.Segmenter throws "compiled without the RegExp engine"

Closes #502

## Plan

**Complexity:** simple · planned by sonnet — The only RegExp use in the segmenter is the locale check at `src/lib/runtime/intl-segmenter.js:215`. A hand-written validator removes it, and a test and a changelog entry complete the fix.

| # | Step | Difficulty | Model |
|---|------|------------|-------|
| 1 | Validate segmenter locale without RegExp, add test | standard | sonnet |

## Changes

### 1. Validate segmenter locale without RegExp, add test — sonnet

`Intl.Segmenter` no longer needs the RegExp engine: the repro program now builds and prints `3`, matching Node.js. In `tests/intl.test.ts`, 22 of 25 tests pass. The 3 failures (PluralRules cardinal/ordinal, and two DateTimeFormat tests) are in code I didn't touch. I didn't run them on a clean `main` to confirm they fail there too.

- **Locale check:** I removed the lazily created `localePattern` RegExp from `src/lib/runtime/intl-segmenter.js`. A new helper, `isLocaleTag`, uses `charCodeAt` comparisons and accepts exactly what the old pattern accepted. The first subtag must be 2–8 letters, later subtags 1–8 letters or digits, and empty subtags are rejected. The RangeError message is unchanged. The file had no other RegExp, `.replace` or `.split` uses.
- **Tests:** Two new tests in `tests/intl.test.ts`:
  - One builds the issue's exact program, which has no RegExp, and checks the output is `3` and equals Node.js.
  - The other runs `""`, `"a"`, `"en-"`, `"-en"`, `"en--US"`, `"en-US-"`, `"e1"`, `"en_US"`, `"abcdefghi"` and `"en-abcdefghi"` against Node.js, which expects a RangeError for each. `"en-US"` and `"en-u-ca-gregory"` must work.
- **Tests left out:** I didn't test `"en-1"` or `"ABCDEFGH-12345678"`. `"en-1"` is accepted by the old pattern but probably rejected by Node's stricter parser, so comparing against Node.js would fail.
- **Changelog:** I added an entry under `## Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md` linking #502.

I ran `npm run format`, `npm run build` and `dist/tests/intl.test.js`. I did not run `npm run check`, per the instructions for this step.

I committed this as `2a4a37d4`. I didn't push.

ci(web): recover a stalled apt download when installing the browser

## What

The `analytics-smoke` job's "Install the browser" step no longer hangs until the job times out when the runner's Ubuntu mirror stalls.

## How

On 2026-10-27, `playwright install --with-deps` / `install-deps` stalled mid-download from `azure.archive.ubuntu.com` three times. On #736, #765 and #764 it held the job until its 15–20-minute timeout, before any test ran.

- **apt network settings.** The step writes `Acquire::Retries "3"` and an HTTP/HTTPS `Timeout` of 30 s to `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/80-ci-network`, so apt drops a stalled connection and retries it.
- **Step limit.** `timeout-minutes: 10` on the step, so a real mirror outage fails as an install failure instead of eating the test's budget.

## Checks

- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm lint && pnpm test && pnpm test:e2e` (CI; `ci-validate` lints the workflow)
- [x] `pnpm db:check` and `pnpm client:check`: not applicable

## Labels

- [x] `ci`
- [x] `bug`

fix(opencode): name the server's error and the early-exit cause instead of a bare status (telemetry 919887a0, d75fcecc)

These two telemetry groups from 0.16.1 told neither the user nor us what OpenCode actually said:

- **919887a0**: `opencode: POST <path> → 500 {…}`. The runner put the first 200 raw bytes of the body into the error, so the scrubber reduced OpenCode's JSON envelope to `{<value>:<value>,…}`. It now reads the envelope (`{ name, data: { message } }`) and reports `→ 500 <name>: <message>`, falling back to the raw body when the body isn't that shape. The POST is still not retried: a 500 is the server's answer, and replaying a prompt POST could run the work twice.
- **d75fcecc**: `opencode serve exited before it started listening`. This now adds the exit code or signal and the last 800 characters of stderr, the same as the existing "did not report a listening URL" error. Telemetry masks paths, emails and quoted values in the message (`scrubAgentErrorMessage`).

Regression tests in `opencode-server-runner.test.ts`, with a `#http-error` hook in the mock server; both fail without the fix.

⚠️ This conflicts with #1573 on one line, the non-2xx `throw` in `http()`. Whichever PR lands second keeps #1573's `OpencodeStatusError(res.status, …)` with this PR's `detail` as its message.

Backport: `opencode-server-runner.ts` is unchanged on `release/v0.16.x`, the line that reported both groups, so this is labelled `backport release/v0.16.x`.

Tests: opencode runner and http suites, 43 passed; `npm run typecheck` clean.
